title: Measuring Electric Field at Interfaces of Fe2O3 and Cr2O3 via High Resolution S/TEM Methods
content: Structural materials in nuclear reactors are exposed to coupled extremes such as irradiation, high temperatures, and corrosive environments, all of which can drastically modify their oxide layers and degrade performance. One of the major challenges for advanced reactors is ensuring that protective oxide coatings sustain their structural and chemical integrity under these conditions. The local electric field (E-field) critically governs ion transport through the oxide and defect formation [1, 2]. Therefore, insights into interface stability, phase evolution, and design strategies for optimizing reactor component materials can stem from understanding how point and extended defects (voids, bubbles, black spot damage), introduced by irradiation and elevated temperature, alter the E-field across oxide interfaces.
